mentions.description: A jewelry line of math, science, and CS-inspired pieces that are beautiful with a (sometimes hidden) meaning. Two styles so far: lambda calculus-based pieces (including y-combinator earrings and an expression that computes Graham's number) and quantum computing circuit pieces. The pieces were previously carried in a jewelry store, whose owner has since retired.
mentions.problem: Marketing the jewelry is the hardest part.

mentions.name: Studio Galois
mentions.description: This project designs and sells math, science, and CS-inspired jewelry whose pieces stand on their own aesthetically while carrying hidden meaning. One style is lambda-calculus based (depicting the Tromp diagram), including Y-combinator earrings and a pendant depicting a lambda expression computing Graham's number; the other is quantum-computing circuits based on the author's physics-professor brother's research, such as a pendant that is a non-local controlled-NOT gate. Production uses a custom DSL the author wrote to describe the pieces, with an interpreter that produces CAD files, then 3D printing or lost-wax casting. Pieces are on consignment in a jewelry store, with museum-store placement in progress.
